question: Does a trained Kintsugi correction improve precision at matched validation recall over frozen Reader v3 and a nonphysical correction?
selection: Training and validation windows of w058 selected using certainty mask only, separated by at least 768 native pixels. Test crop selected by maximum certainty coverage after removing geometry within 20 native voxels of training surface. No ink values or predictions used for these selections.
orientation: PHerc0139 forward. PHerc1447 direction chosen once using the training crop only and then frozen for every split.
normalization: Native 17-layer crop matching Villa. Reader uses original robust normalization, 384-pixel context and 50-percent Hann overlap. Kintsugi receives the same oriented raw CT crop divided by 255, without resampling or Z-flip augmentation.
targets: Human labels only, masked by human certainty. Reader outputs are a frozen input, never pseudo-labels.
loss: FableLoss: equal BCE/Tversky, positive weight 1, Tversky alpha 0.6 beta 0.4. Only the explicitly named fiber variant adds background fiber penalty 0.05.
promotion: Choose checkpoints on validation AP. A correction qualifies for exploratory search only if the two-seed mean validation AP improves by at least 0.01 and precision at frozen 80-percent-recall thresholds improves by at least 0.03 over Reader. Test is opened once after every checkpoint and threshold is frozen. Claim a tested gain only if test AP and precision improve without dropping recall by more than 0.03 relative to Reader.
limitations: Small experiment and two seeds. Spatial holdout within w058 and a separate w060 winding; not a claim of universal cross-scroll accuracy. w062 has public model predictions and no aligned human labels: any apparent text requires publication and expert checks. Fallback axial mixers are convolutional, not Mamba.
